Position Description

The Director of Finance is a senior finance leader responsible for the integrity, stewardship, and governance of ESA’s financial operations and financial reporting. This role ensures accurate and timely accounting, compliance with statutory and regulatory requirements, effective cash and balance sheet management, and robust internal controls. They will be responsible for all day-to-day finance operations, including functional responsibility over general accounting, accounts payable, accounts receivable, pension administration, treasury, investments.

The Director of Finance is responsible for audit readiness by ensuring robust policies, systems, and procedures are in place, and by supporting the external audit process as required.

In addition, the Director of Finance will partner with the CFO, senior leadership, and staff to improve progam or process integration to enhance efficiently and effectiveness in achieving program objectives, In relation to any system or process changes, the Director of Finance will collaborate with respective business areas to positively impact design and operational effectiveness in support of business objectives as well as financial and management reporting objectives.

Role Description

Financial Accounting and Reporting

Provide financial and accounting leadership for ESA’s Finance function and business areas. Oversee all accounts, ledgers, and reporting systems and changes thereto, ensuring continued compliance with appropriate GAAP standards and regulatory requirements.
Design and maintain internal controls and safeguards related to revenue (billings and receipts) and expenditures.
Oversee the preparation and integrity of monthly, quarterly and annual financial reports in accordance with GAAP.
Lead the month end and year end close processes, ensuring timeliness, completeness, and accuracy.
Lead the annual ESA external financial statement audit, including planning, fieldwork and reporting while keeping the CFO apprised of any issues on a timely basis.
Develop, maintain, and enforce accounting policies, procedures and documentation, maintaining an appropriate audit trail for the external auditors.
Monitor and assess potential changes in NFPO accounting standards and or gaps in ESA’s accounting policies and provide data driven, clear guidance and recommendations to the CFO.
Prepare materials for Board/A&IC briefings as part of regular quarterly meetings and/or as required.

Internal Controls, Compliance and Audit

Design, implement, and maintain a strong internal control framework over financial reporting.
Ensure compliance with statutory, regulatory, tax, and reporting requirements.
Act as the primary liaison with external auditors, regulators, and other external stakeholders on accounting and control matters.
Lead the preparation of audit schedules and support external audit activities through to successful completion.
Identify, assess, and mitigate financial reporting and operational financial risks.

Accounts payable and Accounts Receivable

Provide strategic and operational oversight of the accounts payable and accounts receivable functions.
Ensure efficient, accurate, and timely processing of vendor payments and customer billings and collections.
Establish and monitor key controls over disbursements, collections, credit management, and reconciliations.
Oversee the management of aged receivables and support resolution of complex or escalated issues.
Continuously improve processes to enhance efficiency, accuracy, and compliance.
Collaborate with cross-functional business areas on review of manual journal entries.

Treasury, Cash Management & Banking

Oversee daily cash management, bank relationships, and banking structures.
Ensure appropriate controls over cash receipts, disbursements, and account reconciliations.
Monitor liquidity and working capital from an operational and control perspective, in alignment with CFO direction.
Authorize banking arrangements and ensure compliance with signing authorities and delegated limits outlined in the Organizational Authority Registrar.

Investments Oversight (Outsourced Chief Investment Officer Governance)

Provide financial governance and oversight of ESA’s investment activities managed by an outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO), in accordance with approved investment policies, mandates, and governance frameworks.
Act as the secondary finance liaison with the OCIO to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of investment‑related financial information and reporting. The CFO is the primary point of contact for investment-related activities.
Review and assess investment valuations, and accounting treatments prepared under the OCIO’s management for compliance with applicable accounting standards and investment policies.
Monitor adherence to internal controls related to investment transactions, custody, valuation, and financial disclosures, including controls executed by the OCIO and third‑party service providers.
Coordinate with the OCIO, custodians, external managers, actuaries (where applicable), and auditors to support audit activities and regulatory reporting related to investments.
Ensure appropriate investment disclosures are prepared for financial statements
Support the CFO and relevant board committee by conducting a detailed review of quarterly reports provided by the outsourced Chief Investment Officer (OCIO). This includes assessing the completeness, accuracy, and clarity of reporting related to portfolio performance, asset allocation, valuation methodologies, compliance with the Investment Policy Statement, and key risk exposures.
Liaise with the OCIO to obtain clarifications, supplemental analysis, or follow‑up information as required to support informed oversight and governance discussions at the committee level.

Pension And Other Post Employment Benefits Accounting

Oversee accounting, reporting, and compliance related to pension plans and post‑employment benefits.
Liaise with external actuaries, pension administrators, and external auditors on valuation, disclosures, and funding matters.
Ensure accurate recording of pension assets, liabilities, expenses, and associated disclosures.
Support governance and oversight of pension plans in accordance with applicable legislation and policies.

Payroll

Provide strategic leadership and oversight over ESA’s payroll function, with operational payroll processing executed by senior payroll professionals.
Set strategic direction, governance standards, and control expectations for payroll operations to ensure accuracy, compliance, and consistency.
Establish and maintain ESA’s payroll policy.
Ensure robust internal controls are designed, implemented, and operating effectively over payroll processing, payroll changes, reconciliations, and access management to ESA’s payroll system.
Oversee payroll accounting and financial integrity, including review of payroll reconciliations and confirmation of accurate recording of payroll‑related expenses, liabilities, and accruals.
Review and challenge escalated payroll issues, exceptions, or control matters, approving resolution approaches and escalating material risks to the CFO as appropriate.
Sponsor continuous improvement initiatives related to payroll systems, processes, controls, and reporting to enhance efficiency, risk management, and employee experience.

People Management

Lead, mentor, and develop a high performing finance team.
Set clear performance expectations and foster a culture of accountability, accuracy, and continuous improvement and customer service to cross-functional business units

Other

Effectively represent the Finance team as a Senior Management Team Member on board committees or internal committees as required.

Qualifications

CPA designation required
Strong oral and written communication skills.
At least 10-12 years of progressive experience in accounting and finance.
Demonstrated experience in financial reporting, internal controls, accounts payable, accounts receivable, investments and pension accounting.
Experience supervising a team of finance professionals.
Experience with non-government not for profit accounting and a solid knowledge and

understanding of GAAP and accounting for pensions.

Analytic, organization, and problem-solving skills for strategic data interpretation.
Strong emotional intelligence and self-awareness is essential.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills required to effectively communicate complex

issues to senior leadership.

The ability to translate complex financial concepts to individuals at all levels including finance and non-finance managers.

Job Description:

Chef de la Planification Budgétaire et de la Gouvernance / Head of Business Planning & Governance

***English job description follows***

Description de l'emploi :

Vous avez une expérience en gestion de programme/projet, vous souhaitez travailler dans l’environnement du service à la clientèle au sein d’une équipe dynamique et vous souhaitez évoluer et développer de nouvelles compétences? Ce poste est pour vous !

Le programme d'avions commerciaux A220 recherche un Chef de la Planification Budgétaire et de la Gouvernance pour rejoindre notre équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service basée à Mirabel (Québec, Canada), où vous travaillerez conjointement avec toute l’organisation de Service à la Clientèle pour supporter les opérateurs A220.

Vous ferez partie de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte qui est chargée d’assurer une exploitation sûre et économique de la flotte A220 en service. L'organisation de l'équipe est établie de manière à promouvoir la collaboration transversale de manière autonome, en se soutenant mutuellement et en apprenant collectivement.

Relevant du Chef Efficacité de la flotte en service A220, vous contribuerez à la mission fondamentale de l'équipe qui consiste à garantir une exploitation efficace, sûre et économique de la flotte Airbus A220 en service, tout en améliorant en permanence la satisfaction des clients.

Vous travaillerez sur la gestion de la gouvernance des services clients A220 et soutiendrez précisément la performance de la résolution des principaux problèmes en service de la flotte A220.

Votre environnement de travail:

Le siège du programme d'avions commerciaux A220 est situé à Mirabel, dans la région métropolitaine de Montréal, à deux pas de la ville dynamique de Montréal. Réputée pour son environnement paisible et sûr, la région offre une grande qualité de vie aux jeunes professionnels ou aux professionnels expérimentés, ainsi qu'aux familles, en équilibrant parfaitement les opportunités de carrière et les activités de plein air, ce qui en fait un endroit vraiment spécial où il fait bon vivre.

Parce que nous prenons soin de vous :

Avantages financiers: Salaire attractif, bonus annuel, régime d’assurances collectives, régime de retraite et régime d’achat d’actions.
Équilibre vie privée / professionnelle: Une politique de travail hybride, une cafétéria sur site, une politique de congés très concurrentielle.
Bien-être / santé: Programme d’Aide aux Employé.e.s (PAE), programme de rabais et service médical sur site.
Développement individuel: des opportunités d’évolution et des possibilités de formations nombreuses (catalogue de plus de 10.000 e-formations disponibles en libre accès pour développer votre employabilité, certifications, programmes de développement accéléré, mobilité nationale et internationale).

Chez Airbus, nous vous aidons à travailler, à vous connecter et à collaborer plus facilement et de manière plus flexible. Partout où cela est possible, nous favorisons la flexibilité dans nos modes de travail afin de stimuler l'esprit d'innovation.

Vos défis:

Piloter la performance opérationnelle et économique de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service et la gouvernance globale de l'organisation Services à la Clientèle A220 en menant les activités transverses suivantes :
Diriger les instances majeures de gouvernance :
Gouvernance MISP / SISP (Major / Significant In-Service Problems) : Assurer le pilotage de la performance de résolution des problèmes majeurs en service, le suivi du calendrier, la gestion des risques et des coûts, la coordination transversale avec l’Ingénierie et les Opérations en service, et la visibilité mensuelle aux clients avec escalade si nécessaire jusqu'au comité exécutif
Comité d'Arbitrage et de Décision du Portefeuille “Amélioration de la satisfaction client” : Structurer et animer la gouvernance d'arbitrage budgétaire et de sélection des projets (validation des business cases, ROI flotte, critères de sévérité, arbitrages et capacité d'exécution).

Coordonner la définition des indicateurs de performance (KPI) pour l'ensemble de l'organisation Services à la Clientèle A220 et garantir leur parfait alignement avec les Top Objectifs Compagnie (TCO/TFO) A220.
Consolider, analyser et rapporter les performances mensuelles de l'entité, et intégrer ces données dans les plateformes de suivi Airbus pour assurer une visibilité transverse complète entre les différents programmes.
Coordonner la sécurité et la navigabilité de la flotte en service en monitorant les campagnes d'actions de modification et d'amélioration en cours d'exécution.
Optimiser les processus internes de gouvernance, garantir l'adhérence aux standards de l'entreprise et déployer la démarche d'Excellence Opérationnelle.
Préparer l'avenir en pilotant la stratégie de transformation, d'évolution du portefeuille de projets transverses et de régionalisation de l'équipe en soutien direct de la proximité client.

Superviser la planification financière globale (AOP - Annual Operating Plan), la gestion du compte de résultat (ABS P&L) et la gestion des risques et opportunités pour l'ensemble des Services à la Clientèle A220.
Gérer les business cases, le suivi des dépenses et les provisions budgétaires des campagnes majeures de modification d'avions (Aircraft Retrofit), représentant un budget de plusieurs dizaines de millions de dollars
Assumer le rôle de responsable du portefeuille (Portfolio Leader) de projets d'amélioration de la satisfaction client, avec la responsabilité complète de l'enveloppe budgétaire annuelle et des arbitrages stratégiques.
Développer la maturité en gestion de projet au sein de l’équipe Efficacité de la Flotte en service, incluant le déploiement de méthodologies, d'outils structurants et de compétences en leadership.

Votre profil:

Diplôme en ingénierie ou gestion de projet;
Minimum de quinze (15) ans d'expérience dans l'ingénierie, l'exploitation d'aéronefs ou la gestion de programmes, avec un minimum de cinq (5) ans dans un rôle de gestion;
Démontre de solides compétences en gestion de projet/programme, y compris en approche agile;
Solide sens financier spécifique à Airbus Canada et expérience souhaitable dans la gestion d'importants projets multidisciplinaires et de budgets à forte valeur;
Excellentes compétences interpersonnelles, de présentation et de communication pour interagir à tous les niveaux de la direction, y compris la capacité à faire des présentations aux cadres supérieurs (Executives) et aux clients;
Est à l'aise dans des écosystèmes complexes et a une compréhension des organisations axées sur la gestion de programmes;
Est orienté(e) processus et a de l'expérience dans l'intégration de nouvelles méthodes de travail;
Promeut le travail d'équipe et agit avec leadership;
Est axé sur le client et fait preuve d'intégrité en tout temps, sans compromis;
Fait preuve d'innovation, d'engagement et de persévérance;
Une expérience en Airbus et/ou A220 et/ou en services à la clientèle est un atout certain.

En raison du secteur d’activité (aéronautique), de multiples contacts avec des entités Airbus situées dans le monde entier, et d’interactions avec les fournisseurs et clients également situés dans le monde entier, la connaissance de l’anglais est demandée dans ce poste.

Ce travail nécessite une prise de conscience liée à tous les risques potentiels de conformité et à un engagement à agir avec intégrité, ces valeurs sont le fondement du succès, de la réputation et de la croissance durable de l'entreprise.

Donnez une nouvelle dimension à votre carrière en soumettant votre candidature en ligne maintenant !

Trusted Leadership. Public Service That Matters. A Special Place To Live.

An opportunity to support an elected Board, lead a complex public service organization and make a lasting contribution to communities across central Vancouver Island.

With the upcoming retirement of the current Chief Administrative Officer, the Regional District of Nanaimo (RDN) is seeking an accomplished, forward-thinking executive to serve as its next Chief Administrative Officer (CAO).

Located on the central east coast of Vancouver Island, the RDN encompasses the City of Nanaimo, the District of Lantzville, the City of Parksville and the Town of Qualicum Beach, together with seven electoral areas extending from Cassidy in the south to Bowser in the north, and from the Strait of Georgia coast and Gabriola, DeCourcy and Mudge Islands in the east to the edge of Cathedral Grove and Nanaimo Lakes in the west.

Situated within the traditional territories of several first nations, including Snuneymuxw, Snaw-Naw-As and Qualicum First Nations, the RDN recognizes the rich cultural heritage of these communities and the importance of respectful, collaborative relationships.

Home to approximately 170,000 residents, the region is experiencing significant growth. Its distinctive combination of urban centres, coastal communities, rural landscapes, and natural environments creates both opportunities and complex decisions about its future.

Few local government executive positions offer this combination of regional complexity, community diversity, and opportunity for meaningful public service.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the Regional Board, the CAO serves as the organization's senior administrative leader and principal professional advisor. The successful candidate will work closely with the Board to translate its strategic direction into results, provide sound professional advice, lead a capable administrative team, and strengthen relationships across the region.

The role calls for an executive who understands the complexities of regional governance, including the distinct interests of municipalities and electoral areas, the challenges of growth and infrastructure investment, and the importance of fiscal sustainability and responsive public services.

The Leadership We Are Seeking

The RDN is seeking an accomplished public-sector executive who brings:
Professional courage and integrity
— The judgment to provide measured, independent, and evidence-informed advice, including when that advice may differ from the Board's preferred direction.
Political acuity and relationship-building
— The ability to understand diverse perspectives, build trust and work effectively with elected officials.
Strategic and operational leadership
— The experience to translate Board priorities into organizational results while maintaining financial and operational discipline.
Exceptional communication
— The ability to navigate complex and sensitive issues with clarity, diplomacy, and sound judgment.
Collaborative leadership
— A commitment to supporting the Board's governance role, fostering organizational excellence, and strengthening relationships across the region.

What You Will Bring

You will be a seasoned executive with significant senior leadership experience in local government or a similarly complex public-sector environment.

You will demonstrate:
A strong understanding of local government governance, administration, and financial management.
Proven experience leading multidisciplinary organizations and delivering complex public services.
The ability to support an elected Board with balanced, objective professional advice and sound judgment.
Experience navigating organizational change, community expectations, and competing priorities.
A commitment to transparent, accountable, and effective public administration.
The interpersonal skills to build productive relationships with elected officials, employees, first nations, community partners, and other governments.

Above all, you will bring the maturity, judgment and leadership presence to earn trust, support effective governance, and guide the organization through both opportunities and challenges.

Why the Regional District of Nanaimo?

Few executive leadership opportunities offer this combination of professional challenge, community impact, and lifestyle. The RDN serves a region that brings together growing urban centres, distinctive rural communities, remarkable natural environments, and a strong sense of place. The next CAO will have the opportunity to help shape how the organization responds to growth, infrastructure needs, environmental stewardship, financial sustainability, and evolving community expectations.

For the right leader, this is an opportunity to combine meaningful public service with a rewarding personal and professional life on Vancouver Island.

When it comes to health, we’re always looking for ways to push for better. It’s why we were founded in the first place. We aren’t just a health and benefits company. We’re the only non-profit social enterprise that brings worlds of coverage and care together, all in one place.

Description

Job Overview:

The Vice President, General Ledger Accounting
will lead the General Ledger Accounting function for an assigned portfolio of markets and regions. The Vice President is accountable for the overall performance of the GL teams that prepare, review and deliver monthly financial statements and related client deliverables for the communities supported within that portfolio.

Reporting to the SVP, Client Accounting, the Vice President will establish the strategic direction, operating priorities and performance expectations for the assigned GL organization. The role will work closely with market and regional leaders, Financial Management leadership and Client Accounting Shared Services partners to ensure financial statements are accurate, timely and supported by consistent processes, strong controls, effective issue escalation and disciplined performance management.

The Vice President will lead transformation and standardization across the assigned portfolio while ensuring the operating model remains responsive to local market needs, management agreements, governing documents and client expectations. The ideal candidate is a strategic, technically strong and service-oriented leader who can develop leaders, create accountability, resolve complex reporting issues and improve the quality, consistency and efficiency of financial statement delivery.

Due to the global nature of this position, the Vice President should be comfortable working across multiple time zones (Pacific Standard Time to Eastern Standard Time), within reason.

Job Responsibilities

The job duties listed are typical examples of the work performed by positions in this job classification. Not all duties assigned to every position are included, nor is it expected that all positions will be assigned every duty.

General Ledger Accounting

Provide executive ownership of the monthly close and financial statement reporting cycle for all communities within the assigned portfolio, ensuring accurate and timely delivery in accordance with internal policies and procedures, regulatory requirements, management agreements, property governing documents and client expectations.
Establish the portfolio’s operating rhythm, reporting timetables, quality standards, review protocols, escalation paths and delivery-tracking requirements for monthly financial statements.
Ensure the integrity of general ledger activity, including account reconciliations, accruals, prepaid expenses and amortization, fixed assets, interfund and reserve activity, cost recovery billings and other client deliverables.
Serve as the senior escalation authority for complex accounting matters, financial statement exceptions, late or at-risk deliverables and significant client or operational issues within the assigned portfolio.
Oversee GL support for annual client audits and budgets, special assessments, loans, mortgages and other significant client financial obligations.
Establish and monitor service level and key performance indicators for financial statement delivery
Drive leadership accountability for results against service-level and key performance indicators, reviewing performance regularly and leading corrective action plans where targets are missed.
Build the leadership capability, succession plans, organizational structure and workforce capacity required to support client growth, retention and changing business needs.
Attract, develop and retain high-caliber leaders and accounting professionals while promoting a culture of collaboration, accountability, trust and service excellence.

Business Partner

Serve as the senior Client Accounting business partner for market presidents, regional leaders, Financial Management leadership and other senior stakeholders within the assigned portfolio.
Partner with the VP, Accounts Receivable and Resales; VP, Accounts Payable; Senior Director, Treasury Services; and other Client Accounting leaders to ensure cohesive end-to-end service delivery and timely resolution of cross-functional issues.
Translate portfolio performance, operational trends and accounting risks into clear recommendations and decisions for the SVP, Client Accounting and senior market leadership.
Build strong relationships with supported markets to understand local culture, client requirements and operating needs while reinforcing enterprise standards and shared-services objectives.
Act as a senior resource for board members, property and association managers and other stakeholders by leading the resolution of significant accounting and financial reporting matters.
Represent General Ledger Accounting in senior leadership forums, cross-functional initiatives and major business decisions affecting client accounting and reporting.

Financial Planning

Develop and manage the GL operating budget for the assigned portfolio, including headcount planning, forecasts, productivity assumptions and variance analysis.
Align staffing, leadership capacity and workload to the monthly close cycle, client growth, market transitions and service requirements.
Develop business cases and investment recommendations for organizational changes, systems, automation, training and process improvement initiatives.
Monitor portfolio capacity and cost-to-serve indicators and take action when workload or service demand exceeds available resources.

People Management

Lead a team of 125+ associates through a senior leadership structure within North America
Attract, develop and retain diverse, high-caliber talent, while developing an engaged team to build the capabilities required for the organization to perform at high levels.
Promote a culture of collaboration, trust and support.
Clearly define and communicate performance responsibilities, goals, expectations and objectives.
Regularly evaluate teams to determine performance and whether company standards for work performance are met. If expectations are not met, are responsible for coaching and corrective actions.
Conduct ongoing performance management activities by providing constructive feedback and coaching through regular check-ins, structured one-on-one meetings, mid-year touchpoints and annual reviews.

Project Management

Provide executive sponsorship and governance for large-scale GL initiatives affecting the assigned portfolio, including market integrations, client transitions and accounting platform migrations.
Establish project objectives, decision rights, accountability, milestones, risks and escalation paths in partnership with project and functional leaders.
Ensure market and GL team readiness through effective planning, communication, training, change management and post-implementation support.
Provide clear status updates to senior leadership on timeline, accomplishments, decisions, risks, issues and required support.

Business Process Improvement

Lead the standardization and continuous improvement of GL processes, review practices, controls and workflows across the assigned markets and regions.

Job Summary
Reporting to the Scientific Director, the Manager provides operational leadership for the AGEWISE Institute and translates its scientific priorities into coordinated programs, partnerships, and deliverables. The Manager oversees day-to-day administration, research program coordination, financial planning, staff management, funding development, communications and performance reporting across the Institute’s research, implementation and education work streams.

AGEWISE brings together researchers across medicine, nursing, rehabilitation, kinesiology, engineering, fundamental and data sciences, and social sciences to advance healthy aging and translational geroscience. Its mandate connects discoveries in aging biology with clinical trials, community implementation and education to improve healthspan, function and quality of life. The Manager builds the operational infrastructure that enables this interdisciplinary work, including translational geroscience trials, research on accelerated aging after critical illness, and implementation of the AVOID frailty framework.

Job Description
Key responsibilities

1. Institute leadership, planning and governance

• Work with the Scientific Director to develop annual operational plans, budgets, milestones, and risk-management processes aligned with the Institute’s strategic priorities.
• Establish and maintain administrative systems, standard operating procedures, and a coordinated portfolio of Institute-supported activities.
• Provide secretariat support to the Steering Committee and community advisory board, including agendas, briefing materials, minutes and follow-up on decisions.
• Coordinate member recruitment, engagement and collaboration across faculties, Research Excellence Clusters and external partners; organize the Institute launch, member meetings and protocol-development sessions.
• Where applicable, coordinate the approved transfer of Canadian Frailty Network programs, educational resources, digital tools, contracts and residual funds to AGEWISE.

2. Translational geroscience and research operations

• Coordinate a portfolio spanning fundamental aging research, biomarkers, clinical and pragmatic trials, biomechanics, regenerative medicine, and accelerated aging in survivors of critical illness.
• Support the phased development of the proposed Clinical Trials Unit and contract research services, including feasibility planning, staffing needs, costing, workflows, and service arrangements in collaboration with existing research infrastructure.
• Work with investigators and study teams to develop projects, assess operational feasibility, coordinate participating sites, recruitment, and deliverables.
• Coordinate research ethics and other required approval processes with responsible investigators and institutional offices; maintain systems to track approvals, amendments, training and reporting deadlines.
• Facilitate agreements and processes for data sharing, and secure information management with research and institutional teams.
• Support collaborative development of common data elements and core outcomes for geroscience trials, including steering-group and Delphi-process coordination.

3. Healthy-aging implementation and community partnerships

• Oversee program coordination and deliverables for the Public Health Agency of Canada (PHAC) -funded AVOID Frailty implementation initiative, working with the project lead and community partners.
• Build and maintain relationships with older adults, caregivers, community organizations, healthcare partners and policymakers; support meaningful involvement throughout the research cycle.
• Coordinate connections between basic scientists, engineers, and clinician scientists to advance human-ready innovations and enable access to relevant research expertise and facilities.

4. Financial management, funding and sustainability

• Develop and monitor operating and project budgets; prepare forecasts and financial reports; track commitments, expenditures and funding restrictions with institutional finance staff.
• Coordinate grant-development activities, funding calendars, investigator submissions and supporting documentation; assist with budgets, operational plans and non-scientific proposal sections.
• Administer transparent pilot-funding competitions, including calls, eligibility checks, review logistics, conflict-of-interest processes, award documentation and progress reporting.
• Support academic, industry and philanthropic partnerships with the Scientific Director and appropriate institutional offices, including contract coordination, cost recovery and contributions to Institute operations.
• Maintain a sustainability plan and ensure timely sponsor and institutional reporting.

5. People, education and knowledge mobilization

• Supervise Institute administrative and program staff assigned to the position, including recruitment, onboarding, work allocation, professional development and performance management.
• Coordinate trainee opportunities, interdisciplinary mentoring activities, educational modules and workshops in collaboration with faculty and existing academic programs.
• Organize symposia, policy roundtables and partner events; coordinate accessible website content, newsletters, public-facing materials, policy briefs and research communications with scientific contributors.
• Prepare and submit academic manuscripts of Institute’s projects as required

6. Evaluation, accountability and continuous improvement

• Maintain a dashboard of research, funding, collaboration, community engagement, training, and knowledge-mobilization indicators aligned with the proposal.
• Prepare annual reports and briefing materials for the Scientific Director, governance committees, institutional leadership, and funders.
• Identify operational risks, resource gaps and delays; recommend corrective actions and escalate issues requiring scientific or institutional decisions.
• Use feedback from members, staff, trainees, and community partners to improve Institute services and processes.

Qualifications and experience

• A doctoral degree (master’s degree a minimum) in health sciences or life sciences, research administration or a related discipline.
• At least five years of experience in research program management, preferably within a university, research institute, healthcare organization or multidisciplinary research network.
• Demonstrated experience managing budgets, grants or contracts, coordinating complex projects, and preparing reports for leadership and funders.

• Demonstrated commitment to inclusive, accessible and community-engaged research practices.

Preferred assets

Top Priorities

Improve revenue, average cheque, labour productivity, cost of sales and departmental profitability.
Strengthen collaboration among Culinary, Service, Banquets, Sales, Events, Rooms and Finance.
Develop beverage, menu, event and après-ski programs.
Create a positive team culture focused on standards, communication, safety and development.

Review guest feedback and online sentiment and turn findings into clear coaching and improvement actions.
Ensure The Josie's F&B operations meet applicable Marriott Autograph Collection brand standards and guest expectations.
Develop distinct service standards appropriate to each outlet, from casual mountain dining to elevated restaurant and hotel experiences.

Culinary and Beverage Partnership

Partner with culinary leaders on menu development, quality, consistency, food cost, production and kitchen execution.
Ensure menus balance guest appeal, local identity, seasonality, operational capacity and financial return.
Lead beverage strategy, pricing, purchasing, inventory, controls, supplier relationships and team education.
Review menu mix, contribution, waste, yields, portioning and availability; act quickly on performance gaps.

Identify opportunities to leverage combined purchasing volumes, supplier agreements and beverage partnerships across RED and The Josie.

Evaluate opportunities for shared culinary resources, menu development and operational efficiencies without compromising quality or service.

Work with Sales, Marketing and Revenue Management to develop dining experiences, packages and activations that drive incremental visitation, guest spending and destination appeal.
Identify opportunities to improve banquet profitability, event execution and cross-selling between RED and The Josie.

Rebuild People & Culture

Assess structure, talent, procedures and recurring failures; maintain a sequenced improvement plan with both General Managers.
Recruit, onboard, schedule, coach and retain F&B leaders and seasonal employees.
Re-establish pre-shifts, training plans, menu testing, quality checks, labour reviews and manager handovers.
Set clear goals, provide direct feedback, recognize strong performance and address performance concerns promptly.
Build product knowledge, sales confidence, responsible service, food safety and leadership capability.
Create a respectful, inclusive workplace with strong communication and sustainable management coverage.
Build leadership depth at each property, ensuring capable managers are empowered to run day-to-day operations independently.
Develop shared training standards, leadership development opportunities and seasonal staffing strategies where appropriate.
Work with Human Resources to improve recruitment, retention, employee engagement and succession planning across both operations.

Financial Controls Safety and Asset Care

Manage revenue and expenses to budget and forecast, with close attention to labour, food cost, beverage cost and waste.
Review daily sales, discounts, voids, promotions, gratuities, cash, payment activity and operating variances.
Maintain purchasing, receiving, storage, inventory, recipe, portion and point-of-sale controls.
Lead budgeting, forecasting, month-end reporting, capital planning and corrective action for assigned areas.
Ensure compliance with food safety, liquor service, employment, accessibility, privacy, fire and occupational safety requirements.
Protect outlets, kitchens, equipment, smallwares and inventories through disciplined maintenance and asset stewardship.
Maintain separate departmental budgets, financial reporting and performance measures for RED Mountain Resort and The Josie Hotel.
Work with Finance to establish transparent and appropriate allocation of shared costs, labour and purchasing between the two businesses.
Identify opportunities for consolidated procurement, improved supplier pricing and operational efficiencies.
Partner with Engineering and Finance to prioritize deferred maintenance, equipment replacement and capital improvements across F&B operations.

Guest satisfaction, online sentiment, complaint recurrence, recovery time, service timing and quality consistency.
Outlet and banquet revenue, covers, average cheque, menu mix, upselling and event conversion.
Labour productivity, overtime, food cost, beverage cost, waste, inventory accuracy and departmental profitability.

Successful development of a stable management structure capable of supporting two distinct F&B operations.

Education

Experience leading multiple outlets and supervising managers or supervisors across culinary, service, bar and event operations.
Demonstrated experience with budgets, forecasting, labour management, inventory control, menu costing and pricing, and improving financial performance.

Experience with banquets, weddings, conferences and group business is strongly preferred.
Experience with Marriott or another internationally branded hotel is an asset.

Ability to meet the physical demands of an active resort and hotel environment, with reasonable accommodation where required.

Who we need

Reporting to the President, Kilmer Capital Partners, we are hiring a Director, Private Capital Investments. In this role, you will lead investments across the full lifecycle, from evaluating opportunities and overseeing due diligence through transaction execution, integration, and ongoing portfolio management. You will combine rigorous financial and investment analysis with practical business judgment to assess opportunities, identify risks and value creation levers, and translate insights into clear recommendations and action. Working closely with portfolio company leaders, Kilmer senior leadership, external advisors, and a team of two Managers, you will help strengthen businesses over the long term while contributing to a collaborative, transparent, and forward-looking culture within the Private Capital Investments team.

This is an existing, full-time opportunity based in the Toronto office, with periodic travel to support portfolio companies and integration activities.

What’s in it for you?

Impact and investment opportunity. You will play a meaningful role in evaluating new opportunities, shaping investment decisions, and working beyond the transaction to help portfolio companies grow and create long-term value.

Breadth and visibility. You will gain exposure to investments across a diverse range of industries rather than specializing in a single sector. Working within a small, experienced team, you will have direct access to senior leadership across Kilmer and work closely with CEOs and executive teams within portfolio companies, giving you the opportunity to see the impact of your thinking and decisions firsthand.

A broader private capital experience. You will have the opportunity to move beyond a high-volume, transaction-focused investment environment and become more deeply involved in the businesses you invest in. From diligence and integration through strategic planning, operational improvement, and ongoing value creation, you will build a broader perspective on what it takes to strengthen and grow businesses over the long term.

Leadership and influence. This role comes with real scope: leading deals, coaching and developing a team, and shaping how Private Capital Investments works together as we grow. You'll bring your own perspective and judgment to the table, build strong relationships across Kilmer and its portfolio companies, and play a meaningful role in shaping the investment function

Evaluate investment opportunities.

Lead due diligence and transaction execution.

Drive integration and value creation.

The ownership mindset.

Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll lead paid media across Google and Meta, owning capital allocation, measurement, creative testing and the performance marketing team. You’ll use AI to support analysis and challenge spending decisions, applying your commercial judgment to decide where to scale, hold or pull back. You’ll build the decision systems that help the team act consistently and remain accountable for growing sales while protecting contribution margin.

The Problems You'll Own:

Primary: Decide what to launch and where the budget goes:
A multi-million-dollar monthly budget runs across Google and Meta, and every standard campaign type is already live and optimized: brand and non-brand search, PMax, Meta prospecting and retargeting, Shopping and feed. Growth now has to come from what isn't running: new campaign structures, new creative, a different mix of spend.

Secondary: Build the system that runs the scaling decisions:
Design and document the rules that govern spend, when to pause, when to increase budget, when to pull back, and the measurement each decision depends on. The system should run the scaling without day-to-day executive oversight.

What You'll Own:

Capital allocation:
Allocate multi-million-dollar monthly budgets across Google and Meta based on what the next dollar earns, not average platform-reported return on ad spend (ROAS). Bring a weekly recommendation to the CEO showing where to move spend, the expected return and the risks.
Measurement and profitability:
Own one view of paid media performance. Reconcile platform attribution with actual orders and revenue, track the marketing efficiency ratio (MER), and use incrementality tests to see which sales ads actually caused. Measure contribution margin after product returns and financing costs.
Bidding and budget rules:
Build and document rules for bidding, budget limits, and when to pause, hold, scale or pull back. Specify how much evidence each decision needs and when to escalate. Make the playbook usable by any team member before automating repeatable steps.
Creative testing:
Build a pipeline of concepts and briefs. Label tests so the team can distinguish a new idea from a variation, and analyze what gets viewers to stop and what keeps them watching. Apply those findings to the next round of ads, including user-generated content (UGC) and creator-authorized ads (whitelisting).
Retail promotions:
Plan when to concentrate spend around the retail calendar, how to present financing offers, and which messages shoppers should see from first impression through checkout. Test whether a promotion adds profitable sales.
New campaigns and channels:
Launch new structures and creative on Google and Meta. Identify paid channels beyond them, rank each opportunity by its investment case, and design pilots with a budget, a success measure and a clear decision to stop or scale.
Team leadership:
Set priorities, coach and assess senior direct reports and specialists, and develop the skills the function needs. Work with Analytics on measurement and the creative team on briefs. Recommend hires, reporting lines or restructuring to the CEO for sign-off.
AI-assisted decisions:
Use AI to diagnose performance, compare spending scenarios, develop creative concepts, and prepare forecasts and reports. Link the AI review in every proposal to the CEO. Check calculations and creative claims against their sources and own the final recommendation.

In your first year, put the budget rules, measurement and testing routines into use. Start with a baseline and agree targets with the CEO. You can change targeting, bids, creative priorities and spend within approved limits; escalate material risks early and get approval before increasing total spend, committing unallocated funds to a new channel or changing commercial guardrails.

What This Can Mean for Your Career:

Your model informs how much capital the CEO commits to growth next quarter. As you prove where additional spend turns into profit, your scope can expand across the paid channels you select and bring capital allocation, creative strategy and P&L ownership together.

The ability to design incrementality tests, set thresholds and decide when there is enough conversion data to act. Explain how you weigh stopping a promising test too early against wasting spend.
Experience running creative tests at scale since Apple’s App Tracking Transparency (ATT) changes, separating concepts from variations and using creative performance data to decide what to test next.
Experience managing senior direct reports and building or restructuring a performance marketing team. Be ready to show what improved through your leadership and coaching.
A structured way to select a new paid channel, set a pilot budget and decide in advance what evidence would justify stopping or expanding the test.

An opportunity to support an elected Board, lead a complex public service organization and make a lasting contribution to communities across central Vancouver Island.

With the upcoming retirement of the current Chief Administrative Officer, the Regional District of Nanaimo (RDN) is seeking an accomplished, forward-thinking executive to serve as its next Chief Administrative Officer (CAO).

Located on the central east coast of Vancouver Island, the RDN encompasses the City of Nanaimo, the District of Lantzville, the City of Parksville and the Town of Qualicum Beach, together with seven electoral areas extending from Cassidy in the south to Bowser in the north, and from the Strait of Georgia coast and Gabriola, DeCourcy and Mudge Islands in the east to the edge of Cathedral Grove and Nanaimo Lakes in the west.

Situated within the traditional territories of several first nations, including Snuneymuxw, Snaw-Naw-As and Qualicum First Nations, the RDN recognizes the rich cultural heritage of these communities and the importance of respectful, collaborative relationships.

Home to approximately 170,000 residents, the region is experiencing significant growth. Its distinctive combination of urban centres, coastal communities, rural landscapes, and natural environments creates both opportunities and complex decisions about its future.

Few local government executive positions offer this combination of regional complexity, community diversity, and opportunity for meaningful public service.

The Opportunity

Reporting directly to the Regional Board, the CAO serves as the organization's senior administrative leader and principal professional advisor. The successful candidate will work closely with the Board to translate its strategic direction into results, provide sound professional advice, lead a capable administrative team, and strengthen relationships across the region.

The role calls for an executive who understands the complexities of regional governance, including the distinct interests of municipalities and electoral areas, the challenges of growth and infrastructure investment, and the importance of fiscal sustainability and responsive public services.

Professional courage and integrity
— The judgment to provide measured, independent, and evidence-informed advice, including when that advice may differ from the Board's preferred direction.
Political acuity and relationship-building

Strategic and operational leadership
— The experience to translate Board priorities into organizational results while maintaining financial and operational discipline.
Exceptional communication

Collaborative leadership

What You Will Bring

You will be a seasoned executive with significant senior leadership experience in local government or a similarly complex public-sector environment.

A strong understanding of local government governance, administration, and financial management.
Proven experience leading multidisciplinary organizations and delivering complex public services.
The ability to support an elected Board with balanced, objective professional advice and sound judgment.
Experience navigating organizational change, community expectations, and competing priorities.
A commitment to transparent, accountable, and effective public administration.
The interpersonal skills to build productive relationships with elected officials, employees, first nations, community partners, and other governments.

The next CAO will have the opportunity to help shape how the organization responds to growth, infrastructure needs, environmental stewardship, financial sustainability, and evolving community expectations.

Senior Director – Performance Marketing → VP of Performance Marketing → Chief Marketing Officer.

Career progression that takes 4-5 years elsewhere can happen in 1-2 years here for high performers.

The Opportunity:

Puffy is a technology-driven e-commerce business with over $1 billion in lifetime sales, powered by analytics, data and artificial intelligence.Our teams bring together software development, quality assurance, machine learning and AI, marketing, design, conversion rate optimisation, talent augmentation, HR, operations, legal, finance and customer success.

Reporting directly to the CEO, you’ll lead paid media across Google and Meta, owning capital allocation, measurement, creative testing and the performance marketing team. You’ll use AI to support analysis and challenge spending decisions, applying your commercial judgment to decide where to scale, hold or pull back. You’ll build the decision systems that help the team act consistently and remain accountable for growing sales while protecting contribution margin.

The Problems You'll Own:

Primary: Decide what to launch and where the budget goes:
A multi-million-dollar monthly budget runs across Google and Meta, and every standard campaign type is already live and optimized: brand and non-brand search, PMax, Meta prospecting and retargeting, Shopping and feed. Growth now has to come from what isn't running: new campaign structures, new creative, a different mix of spend.

Secondary: Build the system that runs the scaling decisions:
Design and document the rules that govern spend, when to pause, when to increase budget, when to pull back, and the measurement each decision depends on. The system should run the scaling without day-to-day executive oversight.

What You'll Own:

Capital allocation:
Allocate multi-million-dollar monthly budgets across Google and Meta based on what the next dollar earns, not average platform-reported return on ad spend (ROAS). Bring a weekly recommendation to the CEO showing where to move spend, the expected return and the risks.
Measurement and profitability:
Own one view of paid media performance. Reconcile platform attribution with actual orders and revenue, track the marketing efficiency ratio (MER), and use incrementality tests to see which sales ads actually caused. Measure contribution margin after product returns and financing costs.
Bidding and budget rules:
Build and document rules for bidding, budget limits, and when to pause, hold, scale or pull back. Specify how much evidence each decision needs and when to escalate. Make the playbook usable by any team member before automating repeatable steps.
Creative testing:
Build a pipeline of concepts and briefs. Label tests so the team can distinguish a new idea from a variation, and analyze what gets viewers to stop and what keeps them watching. Apply those findings to the next round of ads, including user-generated content (UGC) and creator-authorized ads (whitelisting).
Retail promotions:
Plan when to concentrate spend around the retail calendar, how to present financing offers, and which messages shoppers should see from first impression through checkout. Test whether a promotion adds profitable sales.
New campaigns and channels:
Launch new structures and creative on Google and Meta. Identify paid channels beyond them, rank each opportunity by its investment case, and design pilots with a budget, a success measure and a clear decision to stop or scale.
Team leadership:
Set priorities, coach and assess senior direct reports and specialists, and develop the skills the function needs. Work with Analytics on measurement and the creative team on briefs. Recommend hires, reporting lines or restructuring to the CEO for sign-off.
AI-assisted decisions:
Use AI to diagnose performance, compare spending scenarios, develop creative concepts, and prepare forecasts and reports. Link the AI review in every proposal to the CEO. Check calculations and creative claims against their sources and own the final recommendation.

In your first year, put the budget rules, measurement and testing routines into use. Start with a baseline and agree targets with the CEO. You can change targeting, bids, creative priorities and spend within approved limits; escalate material risks early and get approval before increasing total spend, committing unallocated funds to a new channel or changing commercial guardrails.

What This Can Mean for Your Career:

Your model informs how much capital the CEO commits to growth next quarter. As you prove where additional spend turns into profit, your scope can expand across the paid channels you select and bring capital allocation, creative strategy and P&L ownership together.

What You'll Need:

7+ years in performance marketing, with sustained ownership of at least $1M per month on Google and at least $1M per month on Meta, concurrently or across roles. Ownership means you controlled strategy, campaign structure and budget, even when your team handled execution.
Hands-on Google Ads experience in the PMax era: campaign structure, Shopping feed management, and the different economics of brand and non-brand search.
Experience marketing purchases with average order values of $1,000 or more, where conversions are infrequent and customers take time to decide.
A bidding, budgeting and pause playbook you personally built at scale, rather than inherited. Be ready to present it and explain the business results of a decision you made with it.
The ability to design incrementality tests, set thresholds and decide when there is enough conversion data to act. Explain how you weigh stopping a promising test too early against wasting spend.
Experience running creative tests at scale since Apple’s App Tracking Transparency (ATT) changes, separating concepts from variations and using creative performance data to decide what to test next.
Experience managing senior direct reports and building or restructuring a performance marketing team. Be ready to show what improved through your leadership and coaching.
A structured way to select a new paid channel, set a pilot budget and decide in advance what evidence would justify stopping or expanding the test.
Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed.

Good to Have:

Experience scripting against the Meta and Google Ads APIs, or using Google Ads Scripts.
Experience in both agency and in-house performance marketing teams.
Experience with emerging paid channels such as TikTok, connected TV or affiliate partnerships.
Direct-to-consumer e-commerce experience in home goods, furniture or another high-order-value category.

The Resources to Build On:

Puffy has been AI-first since December 2023. You’ll have company-provided AI tools, including ChatGPT and Claude, AI agents, bots, plugins, AI projects and automations through platforms such as n8n.You’ll also receive relevant department tools, data, assets and specialist support. Use them to challenge a forecast against actual orders and costs before you put the team’s budget behind it.

The Puffy DNA:

We’re ambitious, fast-paced and focused on turning ideas into results.
Be the Owner:
Take responsibility for outcomes and follow work through completion.
Execute with Urgency:
Make thoughtful decisions quickly and act decisively.
Demand Excellence:
Solve difficult problems and keep improving your craft.

Use multi-turn AI conversations to challenge assumptions and improve your work.

Work together when the mission demands it.

Total Annual Package: Up to USD $240,000 + comprehensive benefits (Base salary + monthly performance bonus of up to 20% of base)

Annual salary review every January

Remote First: Work from the comfort of your home office

Eligibility for nomination as 'We Are' Champion of the Month, monthly recognition with gift vouchers and company-wide celebration for exceptional contributions

Position Details

Reporting to the Senior VP, Club & Automotive, this role will provide strategic and operational leadership across QA, Compliance, Business Process Improvement, Workforce Management, membership back-office operations, and the Special Investigations Unit. As a senior member of the Club & Automotive leadership team, the Director will lead approximately 50 employees through a team of direct reports.

What You Will Do

Provide strategic operational leadership across Quality Assurance, Compliance, Business Process Improvement, Workforce Management, membership back-office operations, and the Special Investigations Unit.
Lead, develop, and engage a high-performing team by establishing clear goals and performance standards, coaching and mentoring employees, supporting career development, and maintaining succession plans.
Strengthen service quality and operational compliance through robust monitoring, audits, reporting, dashboards, facility reviews, and adherence to established processes and controls.
Lead workforce planning and optimization by overseeing forecasting, capacity planning, scheduling, intraday resource management, staffing models, employee skilling, and service-level performance.
Oversee critical membership and roadside back-office operations, including contractor payments, membership payment processing, payroll adjustments, claims support, corporate billing, and internal support queues.
Safeguard the membership base and contractor network by overseeing the detection, investigation, documentation, and escalation of suspected misuse or fraudulent activity.
Drive continuous improvement and operational innovation by evaluating business processes, introducing new procedures and reporting, and providing leadership on Business Process Improvement initiatives.
Partner with IT and business system owners to enhance enterprise applications, workforce management technology, call flows, interactive voice response capabilities, and investigative tools.
Provide effective financial stewardship by developing and managing departmental budgets, overseeing forecasts and expenditures, evaluating cost versus value, and ensuring the accuracy of significant contractor payment activity.
Support organizational resilience and service continuity by maintaining effective operating models, High Call Volume procedures, business continuity plans, and operational responses for a 24/7 service environment.

Who You Are

Post-secondary education in Business, Analytics, or a related field.
At least five years of leadership experience, including demonstrated success leading and developing teams.
Strong knowledge of operational management, analytics, business processes, and profit-and-loss management.
Experience with process improvement methodologies, such as Lean, Six Sigma, or Business Process Improvement.
Strong analytical reasoning, negotiation, influencing, communication, and relationship-building skills.
Contact centre leadership or operational experience is considered an asset.
Project management or change management experience or certification, such as PMP or Prosci, is an asset.
Completion of, or willingness to complete, relevant ICMI designations.
Working Environment - This position operates within a 24/7 service environment and may require support during periods of high call volume. Some travel is required for conferences, Club visits, and operations in Manitoba.
